question: For each multi-agent verification in the program, are the agents genuinely independent, or do they share a briefing, a cached input, or a single upstream artifact that makes their agreement a single signal?
title: Independence violation: N agents reading one stale input are one lens

reviewer.notes: Probe 2 re-derives the counterexample from raw input sets and error vectors (Pearson), not from probe 1's Jaccard table or from a prose summary of this report.

method.probe1: Probe 1: compute the input-set overlap between agents for each corroboration event; identical prefixes or a shared briefing artifact reduce N to 1.
method.probe2: Probe 2 (mechanically different): outcome correlation - where the same agents have judged many items, measure their error correlation; near-perfect agreement across a diverse item set indicates a shared lens rather than independent confirmation.

evidence.claim: A distinct-input control pair has low Jaccard and low error correlation, so both instruments can go green.
Copying agent A's inputs and error vector onto agent B collapses N to 1 and turns the calibration gate red.
CNF-0091's biased chair shares a briefing with the sycophant, so chair+sycophant agreement is one lens.
Closed sample of claimed-independent PASS reviews do not record complete distinct producer/reviewer input manifests, so claimed N=2 corroboration is unproven.

control: two agents given deliberately different input sets on the same question must show lower overlap and lower correlation, calibrating both measures
negative control that can go red: replace the deliberately different second agent's inputs and error vector with the first agent's; the calibration gate must exit 1
